_why: Invariant 3 of CLAUDE.md says a number on this site is a claim with an owner, and until
2026-08-04 it carried `(not enforced)` beside it. Checking every figure took a venv, one
git clone and reading two type signatures, and FOUR OF SEVEN WERE WRONG: trailryx said
1,031 tests where the repository ran 1,064, tokenfuse said 513 where it runs 709, engram
said 424 where it collects 466, verdryx said 217 where it collects 292. None was wrong the
day it was written. That is the whole problem: a figure on a marketing page has no owner
and no clock, and the person it misleads is a stranger who cannot check it.
This file gives every one of them both. `scripts/service-numbers.sh` refuses a publish whose
pages disagree with what is written here, and refuses a page that states a figure nothing
It CANNOT check that a recorded value is still true: this repository has no access to the
others' test suites, and a network call in a publish gate trades silent staleness for a
flaky deploy. What it makes impossible is the silent case. What keeps the values true is
somebody running the commands below and writing the date back, and `measured_on` is what
says how long since anybody did.

entries.command: cargo test --workspace, summed; and ./scripts/readme-numbers.sh, which gates the same figure inside that repository
entries.note: Measured 1204 by an actual cargo test --workspace on 2026-08-28; the page said 1,178, twenty-six behind after eight days. Third time in a row this figure has been the one that drifts, and the reason is in the entry below it: the repository gates its own badge, so the number is always true THERE and the site is the copy that falls behind. The strongest entry here: the repository refuses its own push when this number drifts, so the site only has to keep up with a figure that is already true. It did not keep up. On 2026-08-20 the repo gate said 1178 and this page still said 1,172, six behind since 2026-08-10. The repo being honest is what makes the drift measurable, not what prevents it.

entries.command: cargo test --all, summed over every `test result` line
entries.note: Measured 1107 on 2026-08-28 against a page saying 814: 293 behind, the largest gap this manifest has recorded. Found stale by this file's own first run: the page said 513 and `cargo test --all` sums to 709. The gap, not the number, is why this file exists, so it is recorded here rather than only in git history. Unlike trailryx, this repository has no gate on its own README figure, so nothing but this entry will notice the next drift.
entries.check: cargo test --all 2>&1 | grep -E '^test result' | awk '{s+=$4} END {print s}'

entries.command: grep -rhA1 'func (.*) Name() string' internal/detect/detectors/*.go | grep -oE 'return "[a-z_]+"' | sort -u | wc -l
entries.note: Two detectors were added since 2026-08-10 and the page did not move. The command counts DISTINCT detector names, not files: there are 25 non-test .go files and 27 names, so counting files would give the old figure and look right.
entries.check: grep -rhA1 'func (.*) Name() string' internal/detect/detectors/*.go | grep -oE 'return "[a-z_]+"' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' '

entries.command: python3 -m pytest --collect-only -q, in a venv with jsonschema, numpy, rfc8785, sqlite-vec and pytest-asyncio
entries.note: NOT measured here, and the status says so. This machine has no virtualenv for engram and its suite pulls fastembed, which downloads ONNX models, so the drift tool reports MEASURED NOTHING rather than agreement. The figure comes from engram's own README, which its CI gates against a real collection: 517 on a plain install and 524 with the encryption extra. It was 510 here against 511 upstream before 2026-08-28, so it was already a test behind; six manifest tests were added that day. Was 424 on the page and collects 466. One file, tests/test_encryption.py, is SKIPPED for want of sqlcipher3, which has no wheel for Python 3.14, so the true figure on a machine that has it is higher than this. Recorded as the number this command reproduces, with the condition named, rather than as an estimate of the number it would reach elsewhere.

Moved twice on 2026-08-28: 300 -> 361 when the check stopped printing nothing, then 361 -> 365 when four manifest tests were added to that repository the same day. The second was self-inflicted and the drift tool caught it, which is the argument for running the tool rather than trusting the morning's number. Was 300 and measured 361, sixty-one behind. The check printed NOTHING before today, which the drift tool reports as unmeasured rather than as agreement, and that is the only reason the gap was visible at all: system python3 has no pytest on this machine and the interpreter is EXTERNALLY-MANAGED. It now prefers the repository's own .venv when there is one, so the figure is measurable without installing anything.
entries.check: ${PYTHON:-$([ -x .venv/bin/python ] && echo .venv/bin/python || echo python3)} -m pytest --collect-only -q 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '^[0-9]+ tests? collected' | grep -oE '^[0-9]+'

entries.note: Correct. The repository was cloned to check it: 588 swift-testing @Test macros, which is also what its own README badge says and what its CI gates. The one figure on this site that was already right and had simply never been verified from here.

Not a test count at all, which is why nothing could verify it while it sat in a list of test counts. It is a specification constant: the delegation chain in an Agent Passport is capped at 32 entries, `const MaxDepth = 32` in agent-stack-go/chain/chain.go:19, and SPEC.md 5.1 says the same. Recorded here so the next reader does not go looking for a suite.

entries.claim: 88 documented, with whose fault each was
entries.command: ./scripts/gotchas-classified.sh, which prints the total and the four-way split
entries.note: Was `87 documented and already fixed`, and the second half was never true. stack-k8s classifies every entry by whose fault it was, and on 2026-08-28 the split is 39 platform, 34 ours, 11 the stack's own contract and 4 upstream. Only the 34 are `fixed` in the sense a reader takes; the 11 are not faults at all. The count moved 87 -> 88 the same day, when the record profile's first live cluster run was written up. Two more traps documented in stack-k8s since 2026-08-20. Said 70 while the repository counted 79, and the prose beside it said sixty-nine, now seventy-eight. This check walked past both because its pattern knew tests, crates, detectors and entries and the page used a fifth noun: a stale figure sitting inside the thing written to catch stale figures. The pattern is wider now, which is the fix; that it needed widening at all is the lesson.

entries.command: gh api repos/TAIPANBOX/heraldyx/tags --jq '.[0].name'; heraldyx publishes a tag and a GHCR image and no GitHub release, so the tag is the shipped thing and `gh release view` would wrongly report nothing; the page states it once, in `shipped v0.2.2, pinned in the deploy`, where the version IS the claim: it says what the stack-k8s manifests pin, so `latest` would make it false

gh release view -R TAIPANBOX/agent-stack-go --json tagName --jq .tagName; this page states it four times, twice inside install commands, so a tag cut in that repository makes four claims wrong here at once; down to one occurrence, the `go get` line, which stays pinned because agent-stack-go's own README forbids @latest for the library. `go install` of the agent-conform COMMAND is now @latest, since nothing lands in a consumer's go.mod
entries.note: agent-stack-go cut v0.8.0. This one sits INSIDE a `go get ...@` install command, so a stale value here is not a wrong sentence, it is a reader installing the wrong version.

entries.command: gh api repos/TAIPANBOX/scopyx/tags --jq '.[0].name'; scopyx publishes a tag and TWO multi-arch GHCR images, the service and a `-chromium` variant, and the page states the version four times: the spec rail, the header of the measured run, and both docker run lines. The last two are instructions somebody follows, so all four must agree
entries.note: Bumped from v0.1.0 on 2026-08-10 and the measured panel was RE-RUN rather than relabelled: all four requests were sent again to the published v0.1.2 image against a fixture policy, and every verdict matched the row it is drawn beside, including the header refusal, which comes back as a JSON-RPC -32602 naming the argument. Relabelling a measured panel with a new version without re-running it is precisely the fault this file exists to prevent.
